headline: Shifts Data Center Energy Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, including data centers, to pay for their increased grid capacity costs, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Clean Virginia, Governor Abigail Spanberger, Dominion Energy (as amended)
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs
news_summary: A bill is in motion to force data centers to pay more for their energy consumption, aiming to shift costs from residents to corporations and potentially saving residents over $5 a month. Dominion Energy supports the legislation, while the data center coalition expresses concerns about the language.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Requirements
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report monthly potable and reclaimed water consumption by data centers, enhancing transparency on water usage.
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, The Piedmont Environmental Council
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: New regulations taking effect January 1, 2027, will increase transparency on data center water use in Virginia, requiring local water authorities to report aggregated usage data. While specific facility data remains protected, the aggregated numbers will be publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessment Requirements
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and allowing localities to assess other environmental effects.
supporters: Local residents, community advocates, environmental groups, Delegates Thomas and McAuliff, The Piedmont Environmental Council
opponents: Data center developers, real estate interests, industry associations
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass Data Center Siting Restrictions
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153, now passed, establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (HEUF) requiring sound assessments near homes and schools within 500 feet. The bill also grants localities the power to require assessments of potential impacts on water resources, agriculture, and historic sites before approving data center projects.
